intro.default: Hey {first_name}, {rep_name} from Urban Niche — been a while since we worked on {business_name}. Quick reason I'm calling: I'm not pitching you anything today. Genuinely curious how things have been going since we stopped. Got 2 minutes?
intro.training_note: The fastest way to get a former client to hang up is to sound like you're going to sell them something. Open with pure curiosity. No agenda in your voice, no agenda in reality. Mean it.

diagnostic.script: Real talk — when we stopped working together, what was the actual reason? I'm not asking to defend anything. I just want to understand. Be straight with me.
diagnostic.training_note: Shut up after this question. Let the silence work. Whatever they say is valuable — it's either fixable or it's intel on what to do differently next time.
listen_for: Budget — 'it was too expensive' → Ask: where's {business_name} revenue-wise now versus when we were working together? Frame any restart around ROI, not price.
Results — 'we didn't see ROI' → Ask what metric they were watching and what they expected. SEO takes 90+ days to compound — if they canceled in month 1, the expectation was never set right.
Communication — 'we felt out of the loop' → Most fixable reason. Show them exactly what the Monday update looks like now. Offer to walk through a sample.
External — 'business slowed down / seasonal' → Easiest re-activation. Ask where {business_name} is now and what the next busy season looks like.

learning_capture.script: That's genuinely helpful — and that one's on us. If I told you we've specifically fixed [the issue they named] and I can show you what that looks like for {business_name} in 5 minutes, would that change anything?
learning_capture.training_note: Only say this if the issue is actually fixable and you have evidence. Don't promise what you can't deliver. If you can't address what they said, say so — 'that's fair, I don't have a great answer for that' lands better than a weak deflection.

reengagement_soft.script: No pressure at all. But if you're ever open to a 15-minute conversation about where things stand — on our end and yours — I'd love to reconnect. Want me to send over a quick update on what's changed since you left?
reengagement_soft.training_note: A written update they can read at their pace is lower friction than scheduling a call. Get permission to send it. That's the win from this call if nothing else moves.

reengagement_hard.script: Here's what I'd actually propose — restart [service] for {business_name}, but with [specific improvement based on why they left]. Investment is [price]. I can have everything back up and running by [specific day]. Are you open to giving it another run?
reengagement_hard.training_note: Only use the hard close if they gave you a clear, fixable reason AND showed genuine interest during the diagnostic. Don't force the hard close on someone who hasn't opened the door.

last_ask.script: Honestly — when's the right time to revisit this? Three months, six months? I'll set a reminder and reach back out then. Or if you'd rather I don't, just say so and I'm gone for good. No hard feelings either way.
last_ask.training_note: Always give them the clean out. 'Gone for good' removes pressure and counterintuitively makes them more likely to say 'no, check back in a few months.' It works because it respects their decision.
